glossary.Reflux: Backward flow of stomach contents up into the oesophagus.
glossary.Oesophageal motility: The muscular squeezing that moves food down the oesophagus.
glossary.Oesophageal tone: The resting tightness of the oesophageal and sphincter muscle.
glossary.Obesity: Excess body fat, usually a BMI of 30 or more.
glossary.Chronic cough: A cough lasting more than 8 weeks; reflux is a common cause.
glossary.Strictures: Narrowed segments of a tube, here the oesophagus, often from scarring.
glossary.Benign strictures: Non-cancerous narrowing of the oesophagus, usually from scarring after inflammation.
glossary.Clinical diagnosis: A diagnosis made from history and examination without needing a test.
glossary.Meal diary: A record of what and when you eat, to spot foods that trigger symptoms.
glossary.GI bleeding: Bleeding anywhere in the gut, shown by vomiting blood or black stools.
glossary.Anaemia: A low haemoglobin level, meaning the blood carries less oxygen.
glossary.Upper GI endoscopy: A camera passed through the mouth to view the oesophagus, stomach and duodenum.
glossary.Lifestyle modification: Changing habits such as weight, diet and sleeping position to reduce symptoms.
glossary.Proton pump inhibitor: A drug that blocks the stomach's acid pump to cut acid production.
glossary.Retrograde: Moving backwards, against the normal direction.
glossary.Squamous epithelium: Flat, layered cells that normally line the oesophagus.
glossary.Columnar metaplasia: Replacement of normal squamous lining with tall, stomach-like columnar cells.
glossary.Precursor: A condition that comes before, and can turn into, another (here cancer).
glossary.Smooth muscle: Involuntary muscle in the walls of the gut and blood vessels.
glossary.Anatomical barrier: A structural arrangement, here the LOS and diaphragm together, that stops reflux.
glossary.Mucosal healing: Repair of the inflamed inner lining once acid is reduced.
glossary.Acid secretion: Release of hydrochloric acid into the stomach by parietal cells.
glossary.H2RA: Short for H2 receptor antagonist, e.g. famotidine, which reduces acid by blocking histamine receptors.
